subject: Commit minimum, on-demand overage, and burst pricing — hosted API
messages:
From: Alex Reeves <alex.reeves@zenohealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@zenohealth.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify commit tiers / minimum spend / overage/burst rules

Hi Karthik,

We're finalizing our internal budget planning and need a clear picture of Redwood's hosted API commercial terms before we pull the trigger. A few specific questions from procurement and engineering: 

- For usage-based volume discounts (per-token), how do the commit tiers map to per-token rates? Please show an example for a 1M and 10M monthly token commit.
- What is the minimum monthly spend per contract year? Is there a first-quarter minimum different from ongoing minimums?
- If we exceed our commit in a month, what on-demand/overage rate applies? Is that a fixed $/token or a multiplier of the committed rate?
- For short-term spikes (bursts), do you offer a separate burst pool with a capped burst rate or is everything billed as overage?

Can you send a simple term sheet or spreadsheet we can route through procurement? We're targeting a decision by EoQ.

Thanks,
Alex Reeves
Director of Product — ZenoHealth

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reeves <alex.reeves@zenohealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify commit tiers / minimum spend / overage/burst rules

Alex — thanks for the clear list. I've attached a concise spreadsheet (Redwood_Commit_Tiers_v2.xlsx) with concrete examples; summary below so procurement has quick answers.

High-level answers (hosted API, usage-based):

1) Commit tiers & per-token examples (generation tokens):
   - 0-1M tokens/month (on-demand): $0.0012 / token
   - 1M commit tier: $0.0009 / token (committed baseline rate)
   - 10M commit tier: $0.0006 / token
   Example: If you commit 1M tokens/month, committed rate = $0.0009; if you consume 1.2M in a month, 1M billed at committed rate and 0.2M at overage rule below.

2) Minimum monthly spend:
   - Standard annual contract: $10,000/month minimum (annualized commitment).
   - For new customers / pilot quarter we can set a reduced ramped minimum: $3,000/month for Q1 (requires scope + internal approval).

3) Overage / on-demand over commit: two supported behaviors — choose per-contract:
   A) Multiplier model (default): on-demand/overage billed at 1.7x the committed per-token rate for that tier (e.g., committed $0.0009 -> overage $0.00153). Multiplier helps keep price consistent with committed economics.
   B) Fixed on-demand floor: a published on-demand price ($0.0012/token) which applies if higher than the committed*multiplier. We pick the higher of the two so you don’t get a lower overage than published on-demand.

4) Burst pricing / short-term spikes:
   - We can provision a temporary burst pool (subject to capacity) that is billed at a separate burst rate. Default burst pool rate = 2.0x committed rate, capped at maximum 200% of committed unit price. Bursts must be requested ahead of time for guaranteed capacity; ad-hoc bursts fall back to overage model above.

5) Other notes:
   - We provide token-level reporting so you can see commit usage and spikes in near real-time.
   - Add-ons like higher retention or dedicated caching change per-token economics — listed in the spreadsheet.

I've looped in Marissa for commercial cadence; Vivek on the pricing exception if you want a lower first-quarter minimum. If you'd like, I can convert this into a short term-sheet PDF and a DocuSign-ready envelope.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attach: Redwood_Commit_Tiers_v2.xlsx
From: Alex Reeves <alex.reeves@zenohealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@zenohealth.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify commit tiers / minimum spend / overage/burst rules

Thanks Karthik — that helps a lot. A few follow-ups from procurement after they reviewed the spreadsheet: 

- The 1.7x overage multiplier is a bit high for us; our legal wants to see a cap on monthly overage costs (e.g., don't bill more than 2x the expected monthly committed bill) because some months could spike unexpectedly. Is Redwood open to a monthly overage cap (as a % of committed spend) or a sliding multiplier (1.3x for first 20% overage, 1.7x thereafter)?
- On the minimum: our procurement would prefer a six-month ramp commitment instead of a single pilot month—can we agree $5k/month for first six months then step-up to $10k/month?
- For bursts: we need guaranteed short-term capacity for key product launches. Can we get a pre-provisioned burst pool (e.g., 2M tokens/month reserve) with the burst pool billed at a defined rate and rollover if unused?

Happy to take Marissa's or Vivek's input here — procurement needs these in writing to move to PO.

—Alex

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reeves <alex.reeves@zenohealth.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify commit tiers / minimum spend / overage/burst rules

Alex — appreciate the clear asks. Quick proposal from our side to get you to PO-ready terms while protecting both sides: 

1) Overage multiplier / cap:
   - Offer: sliding overage multiplier: first 25% over commit billed at 1.25x committed rate; next 25% at 1.5x; >50% at 1.7x.
   - Plus a monthly overage cap = 150% of committed monthly bill (this ensures a hard cap for surprise months).

2) Minimum ramp schedule:
   - Agreeable: $5,000/month for first six months (Q1–Q2 of contract), then $10,000/month thereafter for the remainder of the annual term. This requires a short approval from pricing but I have latitude here.

3) Burst pool request:
   - We can pre-provision a 2M-token burst reserve for launch windows. Burst pool will be billed at 1.8x committed rate and unused burst tokens do not roll over (we can add limited rollover as a separate concession). Guaranteed capacity requires a 30-day notice for guaranteed capacity; for 14-day notice we can reserve best-effort (no guaranteed SLA).

4) Trial/credits:
   - To help evaluation we can offer $5k in hosted-API credits for your engineering pilot (applied against usage before commit counts).

If that looks close, Karthik/Vivek — can you confirm in writing and we'll seed an updated term sheet and DocuSign envelope for ZenoHealth? Alex — happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk procurement through the sliding overage and burst SLA.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reeves <alex.reeves@zenohealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify commit tiers / minimum spend / overage/burst rules

Alex — Vivek and I reviewed Marissa's proposal and we can approve it as written. Next steps: 

- I'll upload the updated term sheet (Redwood_Term_Sheet_ZenoHealth_v1.pdf) to the Drive link and open a DocuSign envelope for signatures.
- Procurement: please confirm the billing contact and PO cadence. We will set the contract effective date to the date of signature, apply the $5k pilot credit, and include the six-month ramp schedule.
- For the pre-provisioned burst pool, please list your launch windows and we will intake a 30-day notice to guarantee capacity.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
